cost: FLAGGED, BECAUSE HE DECLINED recal_132 FOR EXACTLY THIS: FIVE CARDS RISE BY 8. Kevin Johnson '91 84 -> 92, Steve Nash '03 84 -> 92, Kevin Johnson '90 83 -> 91, Deron Williams '09 80 -> 88, Deron Williams '10 78 -> 86. Nothing on the board moves by 9 or more and nothing moves DOWN at all. This is not avoidable and the arithmetic says so: the ruling itself asks for +7 on the subject (87 -> 94), and every card that rises 6 or more is the SAME ARCHETYPE as the subject — a pass-first point guard at volume 68-80 whose creation runs far ahead of his own shot. If the subject may rise 7 for that reason, so may they. THE FULL LIST AT 6 OR MORE is 24 cards and three families: Chris Paul '07-'15, Kevin Johnson '90-'96, Deron Williams '09-'11, Jason Kidd '03/'04, Isiah Thomas '85/'86, Tim Hardaway '91-'96, Rod Strickland '95-'97, Kenny Anderson '95, Nick Van Exel '00, Steve Nash '03, Magic '85/'90.

THE SEAM COSTS ONE VISIBLE INVERSION AND IT IS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN: STEVE NASH '03 (92) NOW READS ABOVE HIS OWN '05 (86), which is his pinned MVP season. The cause is structural and it is recal_109's line, not this round's: '03 is volume 69 and '05 is volume 42, so '03 is on the hub's side of the 68 line and '05 is on the elite passer's. The two channels pay different amounts at the seam — recal_109's term is worth 10.5 raw to Nash '05 and the hub is worth 6.3 + 2.4 to '03 — but '03 also carries 7 more points of usage on the standard path, and that is what puts him ahead. NO PARAMETERISATION OF THIS TERM SEPARATES THEM: Magic Johnson '90 and Steve Nash '03 are volume 69 apiece, playvol 98 and 90, efficiency 99 and 91 — nothing the round reads distinguishes the subject from the card the inversion is about, so reaching one reaches the other. A ruling on Nash '03 would have to be answered by making the two creation channels continuous across volume 68, which is a bigger round than this one and is named here so it can be dispatched.

THE SIZE MOVED AND THAT IS THE HALF OF THIS ROUND A LATER ROUND SHOULD ARGUE WITH FIRST. recal_55 set the premium at 0.05 x playvol and gave no derivation; recal_98 ramped the gate and wrote that 'the gate, the weight and the class function are UNTOUCHED'. This round changes the weight, and the reason is that the claim now states its own price: a hub's creation IS his load, so it is paid at the load weight (0.26) rather than the creation weight (0.19) and the premium is the 0.07 gap. THE ALTERNATIVE, MEASURED AND AVAILABLE: keeping 0.05 lands the subject on 93 — ONE below his band — with 171 movers instead of 267, a worst move of +6 instead of +8, NO card at 8 or more, the OFF 99-block unchanged at 17 and the top 50 by OVR untouched. That is the round to fall back to if he does not want the size moved.

THE SUMMIT COMPRESSES BY THREE AND THAT IS A REAL COST. Cards printing 99 on OFF go from 17 to 20 — Nikola Jokić '21 and '23 and Giannis Antetokounmpo '22 join the tie block, all three of them bigs whose hub premium grew with the derived size. recal_84 and recal_90 were written to REMOVE exactly this compression and recal_102 reinstated it by his own instruction (1 -> 17). This adds three more. The top 12 by OFF is a pure tie-block reshuffle: every name in it prints 99 before and after.

THE TOP 50 BY OVR CHURNS BY THREE: Joel Embiid '22, Kevin Garnett '03 and Nikola Jokić '21 enter; Kobe Bryant '07, Shaquille O'Neal '97 and '98 leave. Every entrant is a hub whose premium grew; nobody leaves because he fell, they leave because the list is fifty long. OVR moves on 208 cards, max +6, none down.

COLLATERAL IS 267 CARDS ON OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM UP, mean +2.41, max +8: 134 move by 1, 41 by 2, 53 by 3-4, 39 by 5-9. DEF moves on ZERO cards and every attribute on ZERO. The movers are exactly two populations and nothing else — perimeter cards that entered the hub class (creation surplus at volume >= 68) and bigs that were already in it and whose premium grew from 0.05 to 0.07.

WHAT THE ROUND DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO, and each was built and measured first. (1) WIDEN is_big so a rim-leading forward is a big: reaches the subject at 91, moves only 26 cards — and takes LeBron James '13 to 99 against his 97 +-1 pin, LeBron up on fifteen seasons, and Justin Champagnie '25 up THIRTEEN. It also changes the OVR cap branch and the marginal class of every card it flips, which recal_72 warned about at length. (2) DROP the hub's flag entirely: 1,944 movers and NINE anchors broken including Steve Nash '05 at 91. (3) GATE the hub on height >= 79: 139 movers but still breaks LeBron '13 and Luka '23. (4) WIDEN recal_117's volume band to 85 so the elite passer reaches the subject: he reads 92 and it breaks Nash '05, Billups '06 and Stockton '01, because widening the top raises the gate for every card below it. Only the ROLE reading leaves LeBron alone, and it does it for a reason rather than by luck: he is volume 97 with playvol 87, a NEGATIVE creation surplus.

THE SUBJECT LANDS ON THE FLOOR OF HIS BAND AND THE BAND'S KNEE IS WHY. His raw is 95.27, above the 93 knee, where each raw point is worth only 0.615 printed (recal_102's OFF_TOP of 102.75). 94 needs raw 94.63 and 95 needs 96.25 — a further 1.0 of raw, which is HUB_K = 0.104. There is no derivation for 0.104; 0.07 is the gap between two weights that are already in the file. So the round takes the derived number and lands on 94, inside 95 +-1.
data/anchors.json GAINS Magic Johnson '90 off 95 +-1 (round 138), which reads 94 and passes at its floor. Nothing is superseded. 138 anchors, 0 failing.

notes: THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: recal_55's hub channel is a claim about a ROLE — 'nothing priced the offense that RUNS THROUGH him' — and it was gated on a BODY, so the best box season of the best passer in the file lost it the year his three-point rating went 37 -> 60 and flipped is_big's middle shape clause off.

THE SUBJECT DECOMPOSED, and the flag is the whole of it. Magic Johnson '90: BPM 10.1, OBPM 8.3, .622 true shooting, 22.3 points and 11.5 assists in 37.2 minutes, and it printed OFF 87 — FOUR BELOW his own '89 (91). Their raw o_scores are 93.28 [perimeter] and 93.45 + 4.90 [big]. Nothing else on the two sheets differs by anything that matters.

THE ROLE IS MEASURED ON BARS THE FILE ALREADY HAS, and it separates the subject from every star it must not touch. Creation surplus, playvol - volume: Magic '90 +29, Chris Paul '15 +23, Kevin Johnson '91 +21 — and LeBron '13 -10, Michael Jordan '89 -15, SGA '25 -28, Harden '19 -6, Westbrook '15 -5. The men the round lifts are the men through whom the offence actually ran.

THE TWO CREATION CHANNELS ARE DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION, which is this file's own way of adding a term (recal_109 vs recal_112 across playvol 70; recal_131 vs recal_64/107/112 across volume 55). recal_109's elite passer pays nothing above volume 68; the hub's role pays nothing below it. No card can be paid twice for one assist rate, and the whole pure-distributor class — Stockton, Nash '05, the three Mark Jacksons, Billups '06 — moves by exactly zero.

recal_117 DREW THE LINE AROUND THIS EXACT CARD, which is worth stating because it is why he was unreachable. Its own comment: 'the band widens 65 -> 68, set just clear of the nearest star it must exclude rather than on top of him: Magic Johnson '89 is volume 70 and '87 is 71'. The subject is volume 69 — inside the one-point gap between the elite-passer term's ceiling and the hub's floor, paid by neither.

MEASURED BEFORE APPLYING, over the whole family: at HUB_K 0.05 / 0.06 / 0.07 / 0.08 / 0.09 / 0.10 with the role class in place the subject reads 91 / 92 / 93 / 94 / 94 / 95 without the signature and 93 / — / 94 / — / — / 96 with it, and every one of those settings holds all 138 anchors.
